h1: Artificial turf in Ken Caryl, CO, planned around the Ranch's backyard turf spec.
lede: On a detached home, the Ranch's Committee can shape your back-yard turf, but state law says it can't refuse it. Free visit and a written estimate first.
wins: Keep the required landscape around the turf
Choose the use before the product
Plan access across the actual yard

answer.question: What should a Ken Caryl homeowner obtain before selecting turf?
answer.answer: The Ranch's current turf spec, plus any subassociation's sign-off, and for a putting green the Committee's written answer. Backyard turf needs at least a 1.75-inch pile and a landscape buffer around it.

blocks.h2: Choose the product and edges together.
blocks.takeaway: The Ranch reviews the turf product and the landscape around it in one application, so plan both together instead of running turf to every fence. Check the current spec before choosing a product.
paras: Plan the turf and the planting around it together instead of choosing a sample and drawing it to every fence. The Ranch reviews the product and the surrounding landscape in the same application, so the two get decided at once. Check the current specification before selecting the product.

A putting surface is different from lawn turf. Ask the association how it treats a putting-green proposal and which product specification applies before choosing one; the turf standard alone does not establish approval for a putting green. Bring the required application response to the estimate.

blocks.h2: Let the lot shape the work.
blocks.takeaway: Mark your property line beside open space; turf has to fit inside the yard and leave required buffers intact. On a sloped or wooded lot, plan around roots and drainage first.
paras: On a flatter yard, decide how the turf will meet existing patios and planting. On a sloped or wooded lot, include walking access, tree roots and any known drainage or ground concerns before choosing the green’s outline.

Mark the private property boundary beside open space. A green or pet area needs to fit inside the available yard and leave required access or landscape buffers intact. Ask for the proposed preparation and any unresolved conditions to be stated in the price.

blocks.h2: Section 2.05 covers artificial turf. It never says the word green.
blocks.takeaway: Backyard turf needs a pile of at least 1.75 inches, in two to four tones, with a landscape buffer around it. Nothing published names a putting green — ask the Committee in writing first.
paras: Section 2.05 sets the turf spec: artificial turf in backyard applications, a pile height of at least 1.75 inches, blades in two, three or four tones, compatible in color with natural turf, and a landscape buffer around the turf. Side yards are not a flat no; the xeriscape rules put side-yard turf on a case-by-case review (Ken-Caryl Ranch). The rest of the yard still has to hold a balance of planting and hardscape, and rock, mulch and block stay natural in color, so no red or black mulch.

The committee also names what it wants in the packet: a one-foot-square sample of the proposed turf, a site and grading plan showing where it goes, and a landscaping plan with the edging and other materials (Ken-Caryl Ranch). All three are drawn from the same layout, so settle the layout before the packet.

Nothing the Ranch has published names a putting green, so get the Architectural Committee's answer in writing before you choose a product. The Rules, Regulations and Procedures the Committee adopted on June 11, 2026 run to 45 pages and never use the word putting or golf. Section 2.05 sets the 1.75-inch pile minimum with no exception. Section 2.56 covers improvements such as, but not limited to, tennis courts, in-ground swimming pools and multi-purpose sports courts, so its list is not closed; a facility under it can cover no more than 50% of the lot behind the front of the house (not counting the house, landscaping or screening), needs a 10-foot setback and can't be lit for night use. Section 2.42 requires approval for permanent play and sports equipment, which goes in back or shielded side yards where applicable and is reviewed case by case (Ken-Caryl Ranch Rules, Regulations and Procedures). The Fall 2023 Residential Landscaping Guidebook repeats the 2.05 turf rules and never uses the word putting or golf either (Residential Landscaping Guidebook).

What the rules do settle is who decides. An improvement the rules don't list still needs Committee approval, and the Committee's or the Board's reading of the rules is final and binding. The rules say the Committee may grant a variance to the rules if it deems one appropriate, consistent with the Master Declaration. The Declaration section they quote, 8.09, lets the Committee authorize variances from the architectural provisions of the Master Declaration or a Supplemental Declaration when circumstances such as topography, natural obstructions, hardship, or aesthetic or environmental considerations warrant, in its sole and absolute discretion. A variance must be in writing and signed by at least a majority of the Committee's members, and variance requests go to full Committee review (Ken-Caryl Ranch Rules, Regulations and Procedures). None of that says whether a putting green is held to the 1.75-inch pile. So ask the Architectural Committee, in writing: which section reviews a putting green, does the 1.75-inch minimum apply to it, and if it does, will you consider a variance? Until that answer is in your hand, a green here is not pre-approved.

blocks.h2: Approval comes twice a month, and state law limits what it can refuse.
blocks.takeaway: The Committee reviews applications twice a month and can take up to 30 days on complex projects; have approval in hand before work starts. It can shape back-yard turf but can't refuse it.
paras: The Architectural Committee takes up applications twice a month. Most decisions come within two weeks and complex projects can take up to 30 days; approval has to be in hand before work starts, the Ranch asks you to notify adjacent neighbors, permits are the homeowner's job (Ken-Caryl Ranch), and one of the 11 subassociations may need to sign off too (Ken-Caryl Ranch).

State law is on your side out back. HB21-1229, in force since September 2021, lets an HOA regulate nonvegetative turf out back but not prohibit it (HB21-1229), and SB23-178 carries that protection for detached homes today (SB23-178). So the committee shapes how your turf looks; it can't turn it down.

The Ranch's shared open space is a different matter: new non-functional turf is off the table for common grounds under SB24-005 as amended in 2025, while school and district playing fields are exempt (SB24-005).

The Ranch's own Firewise rules land on the same ground as that buffer. No flammable material, mulch included, may be placed within the first 5 feet of a home's foundation; rock, gravel and hardscape are the alternatives named, juniper is not allowed within 15 feet of a flammable structure, and Firewise changes need Architectural Committee approval like any other exterior work (Ken-Caryl Ranch). Section 2.05 wants a landscape buffer around the turf, so where a lawn runs up to the house both rules have to be satisfied in one drawing: non-combustible ground in the first five feet, planting beyond it.

blocks.h2: The hogback splits the Ranch, and the ground changes with it.
blocks.takeaway: West of the hogback, Valley lots sit over tilted shale that moves with the seasons, and a thin base ripples and splits at the seams. We build deeper where the ground calls for it.
paras: The Dakota Hogback divides Ken Caryl into the Plains to the east and the Valley to the west, where Dakota Sandstone caps softer shales tilted at about 45 degrees (Wikipedia). Plains homes from the 1970s and 80s sit on flatter lots; Valley homes from the 80s and 90s sit on larger, sloped lots inside the private open space.

According to the Colorado Geological Survey, expansive clay can grow by up to 20% in volume when wet, and heaving bedrock is its own, more severe hazard, capable of exceptional damage to houses, roads and utilities (Colorado Geological Survey).

On the Valley side, base depth, compaction and drainage under the turf are the whole job: the ground moves with the seasons, and a thin base will ripple and split at the seams within a few years. We build deeper where the ground calls for it.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Ken Caryl, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Ken Caryl, CO. The Ken-Caryl Ranch Master Association allows artificial turf in back yards only, and state law lets it regulate backyard turf but not prohibit it. The Ranch has no golf course, so a backyard green fills the gap. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: What are the watering rules in Ken Caryl?
faq.a: They come from the Ken-Caryl Ranch Water and Sanitation District, which purchases its water from Denver Water (Ken-Caryl Ranch Water). The district's own outdoor rules run from 1 May to 1 October: water two days a week and add a third only when needed, never more than three days a week, never between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m., and repair leaking sprinklers within 10 days (Ken-Caryl Ranch Water). Turf needs none of it, and no rebate pays for it; our water rebates guide lists which providers say so.

faq.q: Can artificial turf go in a Ken Caryl front yard?
faq.a: No. The Ranch's rule is that artificial turf shall only be used in backyard applications. Side yards are the one grey area, reviewed case by case (Ken-Caryl Ranch). State law protects the back yard only, so the front stays the association's call.

faq.q: Who approves landscaping changes in Ken Caryl?
faq.a: The Master Association does, with requests routed by which side of the hogback you're on, Plains or Valley (Ken-Caryl Ranch). North Ranch has its own association around Bradford Park, and a subassociation may add its own approval step (The North Ranch at Ken-Caryl).

faq.q: Does the Ranch's 1.75-inch pile minimum apply to a putting green?
faq.a: The Ranch's written rules don't name one. The Rules, Regulations and Procedures adopted on June 11, 2026 set the 1.75-inch minimum in Section 2.05 with no exception and never use the word putting or golf. Section 2.56 covers improvements such as, but not limited to, tennis courts, in-ground swimming pools and multi-purpose sports courts; an improvement the rules don't list still needs Committee approval; and the Committee's or the Board's reading of the rules is final and binding (Ken-Caryl Ranch Rules, Regulations and Procedures). Ask the Architectural Committee in writing which section reviews a putting green, whether the 1.75-inch minimum applies to it, and whether it will consider a variance if it does. The rules give 303.979.1876 as the Master Association's number for questions about the review process.

faq.q: Is there a drought surcharge on a Ken Caryl water bill?
faq.a: Not so far. At its 22 April 2026 board meeting the district voted not to pass through a surcharge onto customers for the Stage 1 drought restrictions at this time, and told customers to keep following their 2 designated days for watering (Ken-Caryl Ranch Water). Its own outdoor rules page says there are no assigned watering days, so ask the district which applies this season.
